scope: finite-array routing certificate and local guard microbenchmark only

preconditions: q is initialized from the current array exactly
every mutation capable of changing x is mediated and exposes the old and new value (or permits reading the old value before the write)
carrier C is fixed for the certificate lifetime, or counter is rebuilt when C changes
theorem.update_rule: for i outside C, q <- q + 1[new != 0] - 1[old != 0]; for i in C, q unchanged
theorem.conclusion: By induction q remains exact after every mediated write; q==0 iff support(x) is a subset of C.
theorem.two_object_route: For independently mutable state u and Source F, sparse support eligibility is exactly (q(u)==0 and q(F)==0).
theorem.reentry: Unlike a sticky dirty/dense latch, exact sparse re-entry is support-correct after all outside coefficients are exactly cleared, provided the route decision occurs at a canonical synchronization boundary and no stale derived state/cache is reused.

benchmark.implementation: warm Numba compiled sequential set+clear re-entry batches; compilation excluded
benchmark.comparison: counter path includes identical writes + exact counter maintenance + O(1) eligibility; scan path includes identical plain writes + full exact outside scan
benchmark.observed_crossover_note: On this local layout/run, counter path was faster through 65,536 mediated writes per boundary (1.35x at 65,536), but slower at 131,072 (scan/counter=0.68). This is a local guard microbenchmark, not a spectralDNS trajectory speedup.

limitations: Any raw mutable alias or uninstrumented in-place write invalidates the counter and can cause false sparse acceptance.
The current pinned spectralDNS raw-array API has not been shown to provide complete write mediation; R11 already found this missing.
Re-entry requires a canonical boundary with no stale dense/sparse derived state that depends on prior escaped coefficients.
No native spectralDNS/shenfun/FFTW trajectory was executed in this R12 unit.
No PDE correctness, convergence, or universal performance claim follows from this finite-array certificate.
